series_short_description: Growing up in Virginia Beach as autistic fraternal twins, Katie and Nathaniel ("Nate") Prairie build an unbreakable sibling sanctuary to weather school heartbreaks, family storms, and the Blizzard of '96.
series_description: Katie & Nathaniel follows the childhood and teenage years of autistic fraternal twins Katie and Nathaniel ("Nate") Prairie (born April 8, 1985) in Virginia Beach. From secret afternoon cartoon passwords, summer camp at Virginia Dominion University alongside Michael and Rachel Ragsdale, and holiday sofa-bed sanctuaries to the historic Blizzard of '96, middle-school Spirit Week, and their sixteen-year-old summer sanctuary watching Journey to the Sunlit Valley, Nate and Katie discover that while the outside world—and their mother's alcoholism—can be loud and unforgiving, twin brothers and sisters never leave each other behind.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Polls Close at Seven, The 8:42 PM Decision Desk Call, & Victory in Virginia Beach
parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Kempsville & The Virginia Beach Convention Ballroom)
parts.excerpt: On Election Night in Virginia Beach, Nate tracks precinct returns on their custom PHP dashboard until the GNN, GBS, and Beacon News Decision Desks project forty-one-year-old State Senator Katie Prairie as the newest United States Senator from Virginia.
parts.image_alt: Forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her fraternal twin brother Nate hold hands across their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs on a ballroom stage in Virginia Beach with their proud father David standing on his own two feet beside them beneath falling confetti and the GNN Decision Desk projection screen

images.alt: Forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her fraternal twin brother Nate hold hands across their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs on a ballroom stage in Virginia Beach with their proud father David standing on his own two feet beside them beneath falling confetti and the GNN Decision Desk projection screen

parts.part_title: Part 2: The Morning After in Kempsville, The School Tax Referendum, & Jess's Open Letter on The Grid
parts.location: Virginia Beach, VA (Katie & Nate's 50–50 Home in Kempsville)
parts.excerpt: Over morning ginger ale, black coffee, and their daily prescription medication in their Kempsville kitchen, Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and Nate read Jess's viral open letter on The Grid and adopt its eight pillars as her ironclad governing mandate for the U.S. Senate.
parts.image_alt: Inside the sunlit accessible kitchen of their Kempsville home beneath the framed blue butterfly print, forty-one-year-old Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her twin brother Nate sit side by side in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs holding hands at the roll-under breakfast table looking at their open MagnaBook Pro laptop with glasses of ginger ale and prescription pill bottles while their father David stands beside them pouring hot black coffee

chapters.chap_title: The Minified ZIP File, The Raw HTML Takedown, & Resigning from Richmond

parts.part_title: Part 1: The Minified ZIP Trick, Barely Commented Code, & The Live WCAG Takedown
parts.location: Washington, D.C. (Dirksen Senate Office Building Freshman Transition Suite)
parts.excerpt: When the Senate website vendor tries to brush Senator-Elect Katie Prairie off with a ZIP file of minified code, Katie demands the raw unminified repository with the bewildered build team on speakerphone—and both twins erupt in fury over the barely commented, WCAG-failing source code.
parts.image_alt: Inside a Dirksen Senate Office Building transition room overlooking the Capitol dome, forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her twin brother Nate sit side by side in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs auditing raw HTML and WCAG accessibility failures on their MagnaBook Pro laptops over a conference speakerphone while two beltway digital contractor executives sit across the table sweating and shell-shocked

images.alt: Inside a Dirksen Senate Office Building transition room overlooking the Capitol dome, forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her twin brother Nate sit side by side in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs auditing raw HTML and WCAG accessibility failures on their MagnaBook Pro laptops over a conference speakerphone while two beltway digital contractor executives sit across the table sweating and shell-shocked

parts.part_title: Part 2: Article IV Section 4, Hand-Delivering Her Resignation in Richmond, & The Writ of Special Election
parts.location: Richmond, VA (The Virginia State Capitol & The Office of the Clerk of the Senate of Virginia)
parts.excerpt: Because Article IV, Section 4 of the Constitution of Virginia forbids holding both a state legislative seat and federal office, State Senator Katie Prairie travels to the Virginia State Capitol in Richmond with Nate to formally hand-deliver her resignation to the Clerk of the Senate.
parts.image_alt: Inside the historic neoclassical Clerk's Office of the Senate of Virginia at the State Capitol in Richmond, forty-one-year-old State Senator and U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie sits in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair alongside her twin brother Nate in his matching powerchair and formally hands her gold-sealed parchment resignation letter across the mahogany counter to the Clerk of the Senate

images.alt: Inside the historic neoclassical Clerk's Office of the Senate of Virginia at the State Capitol in Richmond, forty-one-year-old State Senator and U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie sits in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair alongside her twin brother Nate in his matching powerchair and formally hands her gold-sealed parchment resignation letter across the mahogany counter to the Clerk of the Senate

chapters.chap_title: First Train from Norfolk & Swearing In on the Constitution

parts.part_title: Part 1: Three Business Class Tickets for Free Café Car Drinks & The Mobile Lift at Alexandria
parts.location: Norfolk & Alexandria, VA (Norfolk Station NFK, ARTS Northeast Regional, & Alexandria Union Station ALX)
parts.excerpt: On the morning of her U.S. Senate swearing-in, forty-one-year-old Senator-Elect Katie Prairie, her twin brother Nate, and their dad David ride the 5:00 AM ARTS Business Class train from Norfolk for the free Café Car drinks—and shock commuters by detraining on the mobile lift at Alexandria instead of Washington Union Station.
parts.image_alt: Forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie sits in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair on the yellow-and-silver ARTS Mobile Lift outside the open ARTS Business Class door at Alexandria Union Station while her twin brother Nate in his matching powerchair holding a Café Car cup and their proud father David wait on the low-level red-brick platform below

images.alt: Forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator-Elect Katie Prairie sits in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair on the yellow-and-silver ARTS Mobile Lift outside the open ARTS Business Class door at Alexandria Union Station while her twin brother Nate in his matching powerchair holding a Café Car cup and their proud father David wait on the low-level red-brick platform below

Forty-one-year-old Senator-Elect Katie Prairie and her twin brother Nate roll side by side in their compact SwiftChair power wheelchairs holding hands down the open-air red-brick platform of historic Alexandria Union Station with their proud father David walking beside them under the clear winter sky and the George Washington Masonic National Memorial on the hill

parts.part_title: Part 2: The Yellow Line Over the Fenwick Bridge, The Full-Chair Portrait, & Swearing In on the Constitution
parts.location: Alexandria, VA & Washington, D.C. (King St–Old Town Metro, Charles R. Fenwick Bridge, L'Enfant Plaza, Capitol South, & The United States Senate)
parts.excerpt: Proving her transit-insider credentials by taking the Capital Transit Yellow Line across the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge to L'Enfant Plaza instead of the long Blue Line detour via Rosslyn, Katie refuses to hide her powerchair in her official Senate portrait and swears her oath on the Constitution of the United States of America.
parts.image_alt: Official full-seated U.S. Senate portrait of forty-one-year-old U.S. Senator Katie Prairie of Virginia proudly seated in her compact SwiftChair power wheelchair in a royal-blue blazer between the United States and Virginia flags with the Capitol dome visible through the arched window behind her

parts.part_title: Part 3: The First Invite to Cocktails, A Known Side Effect of Death, & Home to Sunset Drive
parts.location: Washington, D.C. & Alexandria, VA (The Mansfield Room at the U.S. Capitol, Capital Transit Yellow Line, & The Brick House on Sunset Drive)
parts.excerpt: Invited to her first Senate leadership cocktail reception, Senator Katie Prairie establishes that she, Nate, and their dad take a daily medication where mixing with alcohol or tobacco has a known side effect of death—before riding the Yellow Line back to their two-story brick house on Sunset Drive.
